title: The thick lines are gone - before | after, all ten
question: Are the late thick lines fixed, and does #3 now do enough?
context_md:
The same ten, each one **before on the left and after on the right, playing together**. Same seed, same framing, same noon lighting.

**The thick lines are gone, and they were one mechanism.** Three things in the game draw cracks: the new fabric draws one cell wide, the pick and chisel draw one cell wide, and one old path drew *two* - it marked an edge and its mirror. That path also wandered by 0.9 radians per cell (the scribble you rejected), fired hundreds of frames late off a wavefront crawling at one cell per five frames, and drew its whole star in a *single frame*. Thick, scribbly, late, and popping in rather than spreading - your four descriptions were one bug. It now reveals the same grain everything else does.

I proved it before changing anything, using a switch that already ships: with that path off, cracked cells in the world fell 610 to 145, unsupported judgements 2,365 to 29, and *more* material moved. It was almost pure noise.

**#3 should now do something** - surface and shallow shots were starved because confinement *gated* how much rock cracked. It now scales instead, so buried still cracks more but a surface shot cracks a real web. Buried-to-surface went from 5.8:1 to 1.8:1, and every already-good buried charge is bit-identical (#1, #6, #7, #8, #9, #10 unchanged). An airburst still does **not** dice the ground under it - I checked, since that was the obvious way to get this wrong.

**Where it settles matters more than any single frame.** The old path never terminated: promoted cells at frames 900/1100/1300 were 2,184 / 2,226 / 2,710 and still climbing. Now it is 1,213 / 1,213 / 1,213 - settled. Across four seeds the *worst* case for material actually moving is up 50% (6,043 to 9,042), and the worst frame went 104ms to 73ms.

**Two honest costs.** A heavy pick blow on a hillside now removes more rock than it did last week - back to roughly where this branch started, having dipped in between. And the crack pattern still arrives in one frame rather than growing; there is far less of it and it is aligned to the grain, but 'spreads rather than pops' is only half done.

Ignore the trees and the grain.
